assets.editPrompt: Edit the attached empty house sprite. Critical correction: the BOTTOM / SOUTH wall currently shows its EXTERIOR face, so only three INTERIOR wall faces are visible. Rebuild ONLY that bottom wall and its two corner joins so we see its INNER face looking toward the center of the room, symmetrically opposite the top wall. Concrete geometry: the TOP CAP / topmost horizontal beam of the south wall belongs at the very BOTTOM OUTER edge of the image, around 94% canvas height. Its visible plaster/masonry INNER FACE must extend UPWARD from that cap toward the floor, occupying about 82%–94% canvas height. The baseboard / foot of the south wall is at about 82% height where it touches the floor. Do NOT leave a horizontal beam at 82% height with the wall face hanging BELOW it: that is an EXTERIOR facade and is the error to correct. The south wall should splay outward at its corners: inner floor corners about x14% and86% at y82%; outer cap corners about x5% and95% at y94%. Preserve an open doorway centered in the south wall, with the jambs and threshold also rebuilt in the corrected inward-facing perspective. Viewer should be able to stand at the CENTER of the room and see the four surfaces all facing them: north, south, east and west. Keep top/left/right walls, windows, material style, high-quality texture, original square proportions, floor and transparency outside the building. Keep room completely empty. No text or furniture. This is a symmetric overhead cutaway / splayed-wall battlemat, NOT an oblique camera viewing only the three far walls. For unambiguous geometry, the south wall must look exactly like the NORTH wall rotated 180 degrees and fitted around the open doorway: its wide wall TOP CAP is on the OUTER bottom edge, its INNER FACE and structural studs are ABOVE the cap, its baseboard is above the face against the wooden floor. Make all four wall planes symmetrically splayed away from the room centre. Do not show the outside facade of the south wall.
